outcome: Give logistics coo / supply chain director a governed method to improve units picked per labour hour using SKU velocity, aisle maps and picker journeys, with final decisions retained by named staff.
overview: Warehouse Slotting and Pick Path Optimisation addresses resource allocation is planned in silos, producing avoidable delays and occasionally infeasible instructions in logistics and supply chain operations. The first proof of value uses SKU velocity, aisle maps and picker journeys. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is units picked per labour hour, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: SKU velocity, aisle maps and picker journeys; define units picked per labour hour and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Logistics COO / Supply Chain Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including replay disruption and edge cases with hard constraints enforced.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for units picked per labour hour
